answer: Require each agent identity to be backed by a verifiable work history: a newcomer starts at the bottom of a canyon of trust and must complete a sequence of small, publicly audited tasks before it can trade. Like a raven earning its place in a flock through repeated useful flights, reputation accrues slowly and is non-transferable. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the full cost of that climb for every single one, while a legitimate agent reaches its zenith of privileges only after sustained honest work, making sybil creation expensive and unprofitable.
